title: OpenAI acquires Ona to give Codex long-running, customer-controlled cloud execution
summary: OpenAI announced on June 11, 2026, that it will acquire Ona, a startup whose technology provides secure, persistent cloud environments where AI agents can access tools, systems, and context over time; Ona's customer-controlled execution model will let Codex agents operate inside an organization's own cloud while OpenAI provides the intelligence and orchestration, with the Ona team joining OpenAI's Codex group after closing.

title: OpenAI and Visa embed agentic payments inside ChatGPT for any merchant on the network
summary: OpenAI and Visa announced a partnership on June 11, 2026, that lets ChatGPT shop and complete purchases on behalf of users at any merchant that accepts Visa, with tokenized credentials, spending limits, required approvals, and merchant allowlists; the framework also exposes the rails to developers and merchants via OpenAI's agentic commerce protocol.

title: OpenAI ships models and Codex through Oracle Cloud, letting enterprises draw down existing commitments
summary: OpenAI announced on June 11, 2026, that its models and the Codex coding agent are now available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, letting enterprise customers apply existing Oracle Cloud commitments to OpenAI usage and avoid fresh procurement cycles; the arrangement turns Oracle into a first-class OpenAI distribution channel alongside Microsoft Azure.

title: Anthropic and DXC Technology form multi-year alliance to deploy Claude inside banks, airlines, and government
summary: Anthropic and DXC Technology announced a multi-year global alliance on June 11, 2026, in which DXC will train tens of thousands of Claude-certified forward-deployed engineers to bring Claude into the systems DXC operates for the world's largest banks, airlines, insurers, manufacturers, and government agencies, starting with Modernization-as-a-Service, cybersecurity, and OASIS-based application services.

title: Anthropic taps TCS to scale Claude across Indian enterprises, financial services, and Diligenta
summary: Anthropic partnered with Tata Consultancy Services on June 11, 2026, to set up a dedicated business unit for deploying Claude to TCS customers, give more than 50,000 TCS employees access to Claude, and build out Diligenta (22M+ UK life-and-pensions customers) and TCS iON on top of the Claude Code ecosystem.

title: Anthropic apologizes and walks back invisible distillation guardrails on Claude Fable 5
summary: Anthropic apologized on June 11, 2026, for stealthily throttling Claude Fable 5 with hidden guardrails that blocked research and competitor distillation queries, saying the company will now fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 and tell users every time a safeguard is triggered; the reversal follows backlash from the AI research community and Wired's reporting on the policy.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Corps, a national fellowship to extend AI benefits across American communities
summary: Anthropic announced Claude Corps on June 11, 2026, a national fellowship program for people early in their careers who are passionate about extending the benefits of AI to communities across America; the program sits alongside DXC, TCS, Project Glasswing, and the new policy push as Anthropic builds enterprise and civic distribution for Claude.

title: Google DeepMind commits $10M with Schmidt Sciences, ARIA, and Cooperative AI to study multi-agent safety
summary: Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences, ARIA, the Cooperative AI foundation, and Google.org announced a $10 million research fund on June 11, 2026, to seed academic work on how millions of AI agents will behave when they interact across the open internet; DeepMind's AGI safety lead Rohin Shah says the field of multi-agent safety effectively does not exist yet and the timing is urgent.

title: Google releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B open diffusion language model that runs on 18GB of RAM
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled DiffusionGemma on June 11, 2026, an experimental 26-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model that generates paragraphs of tokens in parallel using diffusion rather than autoregressive decoding, posting up to 4x speedup on a single H100 and running locally on 18GB of DRAM or VRAM; the open-weights model is released under Apache 2.0 with vLLM, MLX, and HF Transformers support.

title: xAI launches Grok Build Plugin Marketplace with MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, and Cloudflare
summary: xAI launched the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace on June 11, 2026, a built-in catalog of plugins that bundle skills, slash commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and LSPs into a single installable package; the launch catalog ships six partners and pins every remote plugin to a 40-character commit SHA that Grok Build re-verifies after cloning.

title: Canada's Privacy Commissioner finds xAI and X violated federal law on Grok sexualized deepfakes
summary: Canada's Privacy Commissioner of Canada released a report on June 11, 2026, finding that X Corp. and xAI violated Canada's federal private-sector privacy law by launching the Grok image-generation tool without proper safeguards, fueling millions of non-consensual sexualized deepfakes; the Commissioner welcomed xAI's subsequent mitigations but lacks authority to fine or order changes.

title: NVIDIA unveils Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot with Unitree, Sharpa Wave, and Jetson Thor
summary: NVIDIA unveiled the Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot at GTC Taipei on June 11, 2026, a fully open humanoid platform combining a Unitree H2 Plus body, Sharpa Wave five-finger tactile hands, Jetson Thor onboard compute, and the full Isaac GR00T software stack; the platform also adds Unitree G1 support and is expected from Unitree in late 2026.

title: NVIDIA launches Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) for autonomous manufacturing agents
summary: NVIDIA announced the Factory Operations Blueprint, or FOX, at GTC Taipei on June 11, 2026, a reference design for building autonomous factory manager agents that connect machine data, quality systems, work instructions, robot fleets, and operational alerts into one AI-driven decision layer; the blueprint is built on NemoClaw, AI-Q Blueprint, and Nemotron open models.

title: Lionsgate takes equity stake in Runway, joint development to mine franchises for AI-generated shorts
summary: Runway and Lionsgate announced an expanded partnership on June 11, 2026, in which Lionsgate has taken an equity interest in Runway and the two companies will launch a joint development program to co-produce new IP, starting with a short-form episodic series drawing on Lionsgate's franchises; Lionsgate also becomes a presenting partner at the Runway AI Festival in June.

title: Perplexity moves Deep Research into Computer, routing subtasks across 20+ frontier models
summary: Perplexity moved Deep Research into its Computer multi-model orchestration system on June 11, 2026, breaking hard questions into subtasks and routing them across 20+ frontier models to produce reports, decks, and dashboards; BrowseComp accuracy jumped from 40.7% to 83.8% and Humanity's Last Exam rose 36.4% to 50.5%, with Search-as-Code available through both Computer and the Agent API.

title: Perplexity and Amazon face skeptical Ninth Circuit panel over Comet shopping agent injunction
summary: A Ninth Circuit panel heard arguments on June 11, 2026, over whether to keep a preliminary injunction blocking Perplexity's Comet browser from shopping on Amazon, with judges pushing back on Perplexity's argument that agents gain authorized access through their users; the ACLU filed an amicus brief warning a ruling for Amazon could chill journalism, research, and common browser tools.

title: Hugging Face ships PhysicsIntern 2.0 as a set of skills that ride on Claude Code, Codex, and Pi
summary: Hugging Face published PhysicsIntern 2.0 on June 11, 2026, rebuilding the autonomous physics-research agent as a set of skills rather than a bespoke harness, so it runs on top of Claude Code, Codex, and Pi with surveyor, deriver, computer, reviewer, critic, and finalizer sub-agents in fresh contexts and at least two independent verdicts required before a result is treated as established.

title: Hugging Face and Arcee sign multi-million-dollar deal to make the Hub Arcee's exclusive storage home
summary: Hugging Face announced a multi-million-dollar strategic collaboration on June 9, 2026, making the Hugging Face Hub the exclusive home for all of Arcee AI's models, datasets, and agent traces (public and private) via the new Buckets private-storage product; the deal gives Arcee a cloud-agnostic store where it can train on any provider without egress fees or lock-in.

title: Zhipu and Tsinghua release SCAIL-2, an end-to-end video model that abandons stick-figure intermediates
summary: Zhipu AI and the Tsinghua University team led by Professor Tang Jie released SCAIL-2 on June 11, 2026, an end-to-end video model that abandons the industry's reliance on explicit intermediate 'stick-figure' pose representations and instead drives latent-space features directly, framing the model as a 'driver program' for the AGI operating system and a paradigm challenge to current digital content pipelines.

title: Apple debuts third-generation Apple Foundation Models built with Google, on-device and Private Cloud Compute
summary: At WWDC 2026, Apple introduced five third-generation Apple Foundation Models custom-built with Google, spanning two on-device variants (3B dense AFM 3 Core and 20B sparse AFM 3 Core Advanced activating 1–4B params) and three Private Cloud Compute server models (AFM 3 Cloud, ADM 3 Cloud Image, AFM 3 Cloud Pro) that power Siri AI, Image Playground, expressive voices, and agentic tool use across iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, and visionOS 27.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 with 30-day safety retention
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 as the first publicly available Mythos-class model on $10/$50 per million input/output tokens, with Claude Mythos 5 reserved for Project Glasswing cyber partners and trusted biology researchers; Anthropic also announced a 30-day data retention policy for both models, even for zero-retention enterprise customers.

title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi Work, a desktop agent that runs 300 specialized agents in parallel
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi Work, a Windows and macOS desktop agent that orchestrates up to 300 specialized sub-agents over the Agent Swarm architecture introduced with Kimi K2.6; the product combines local folder access, autonomous web navigation, background Python execution, scheduled tasks, and a memory layer that retains preferences across sessions.

title: Meta's Muse Spark AI replaces Llama 4 across Ray-Ban and Oakley smart glasses
summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs extended its Muse Spark model to all Ray-Ban and Oakley smart glasses except Meta Ray-Ban Display; Muse Spark matches Llama 4 Maverick performance at 10x lower compute, is closed-source, and Meta has delayed the public API multiple times since April while targeting a release within June.

title: Zhipu launches GLM-5.1 with 8-hour autonomous work mode and 10% price hike
summary: Zhipu released GLM-5.1 with a new '8-hour work mode' that lets the model independently plan, execute, test, and self-repair across a single task, becoming the first domestic model to top Opus 4.6 on SWE-bench Pro; pricing rose 10%, reaching parity with Anthropic in coding scenarios as the company pivots from price competition to long-duration agent execution.
